design-code-rules.title: Bi-directional cycle route – route
design-code-rules.requirement-text: A segregated two-way cycle track should run at footway level along the whole eastern side of the A23, between the footway and the carriageway.
design-code-rules.guidance-text:
The aim is a continuous, segregated two-way cycle track along the whole eastern side of the A23, better for both walking and cycling than the shared footways along much of the route today. Any changes to the corridor should at least meet LTN 1/20, and some dimensions here go further.
Worked examples: Example 1: South Horley; Example 2: South Salfords; Example 3: Brighton Road, southern approach to Redhill; Example 5: Brighton Road through Salfords

design-code-rules.title: Street furniture, pedestrian guardrail and seating – furniture zone

design-code-rules.guidance-text:

design-code-rules.title: Carriageway design, surfacing, signage and markings – lane widths
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Traffic lanes between 3.2m and 3.9m wide should not be used; the preferred lane is 3.2m, giving a 6.4m carriageway on most of the route.
design-code-rules.guidance-text:
Lanes between 3.2m and 3.9m let drivers pass cyclists closely without crossing the centre line. Removing centre lines has been shown to reduce speeds, and sparing use of signs, backing boards and coloured surfacing reduces clutter.
Worked examples: Example 1: South Horley; Example 2: South Salfords; Example 3: Brighton Road, southern approach to Redhill; Example 5: Brighton Road through Salfords

design-code-rules.title: Junction design and spacing – continuous crossings
design-code-rules.requirement-text: Continuous crossings should be used wherever a side street carrying fewer than 2,000 vehicles a day meets the A23; crossroads or slightly staggered junctions are encouraged.
design-code-rules.guidance-text:
Tight corners slow turning vehicles and help people cross. Manual for Streets 2 found no evidence that junctions with less visibility than standard have more collisions, and longer sight lines can even increase risk. Right-turn lanes and large roundabouts are trunk-road features that make crossing harder.
Worked examples: Example 3: Brighton Road, southern approach to Redhill
